[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] CooperBench 检查两个.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] CooperBench checks whether two coding agents can combine their respective modifications into a correct program. The authors' selection rules are effective for held-out configurations but cannot reliably predict absolute scores in entirely new task domains. Each configuration in SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench only tests 20 questions, and about 45% of baseline thresholds are based on empirical rules.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 同一模型的解决率随 harness 改.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The success rate of the same model varies with the harness, with a maximum difference of 44 percentage points, and the harness ranking also changes with the model. Different frameworks also have their own execution limits and timeouts, so these differences correspond to the full actual tested configurations in the paper.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 在 ProgramBench 的一组同.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] In a set of matched comparisons in ProgramBench, only delegated planning can achieve scores close to full-stage delegation at lower cost; the stage benefits of Commit0-Lite differ, so "only delegate planning is the best" cannot be generalized to all coding tasks. [\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 作者在 MACS、ConVerse 和.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The authors compared smolagents, LangGraph, and LlamaIndex in selected scenarios of MACS, ConVerse, and MultiAgentBench, using GPT-5-mini, Gemini-3.0-Flash, and Claude-Haiku-4.5. Within similar capability and cost tiers, framework choices can also significantly change the results. It provides a cross-framework evaluation interface, while specific tasks are still defined by the connected benchmark; supporting a particular adapter does not mean that the paper has fully reproduced all scenarios in that benchmark.

Each trajectory only examines predefined interventions, such as adding markers that must be preserved in upstream messages, checking step by step whether they reach downstream. Other tests record the loss of hard constraints, propagation of incorrect facts, and cross-task information leakage. The experiments involve controlled message interactions, and the original text does not disclose the inference engine or hardware. [\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 在 Doc2Repo、NL2Repo、.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] In the tasks of generating repositories from specifications in Doc2Repo, NL2Repo, and CodeProjectEval, authors report that compared to free-message teams, test pass rates are higher and full task times are shorter. [\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] AssistantBench、GAIA.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] Empirical results on AssistantBench and GAIA show that filtering shared results can reduce duplicated execution and, in some settings, balance quality and overall task time. For hidden state X, the value can be written as [[A0]] — XW₀ is the base projection, XA is the low-dimensional intermediate result, which, after multiplying by B, produces the role increment.

OpenCollab separates "how to organize roles" from "how to invoke models and tools," allowing different organizational methods to share the same execution backbone, facilitating the control of experimental conditions.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 同模型、同任务和预算下，团队有时提高通.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] Under the same model, same task, and same budget, teams sometimes improve pass rates, while a single-agent configuration may save more tokens and costs; correct execution of the structure does not guarantee final success. The paper provides comparisons on SWE-Bench Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and DeepSWE. It primarily offers an implementation and auditing framework for organizational methods and should not be used to infer the effectiveness of collaboration mechanisms based solely on role names or a single result.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] Helium 处理结构相同、输入.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] Helium handles a batch of agent workflows that have the same structure but different inputs. Users first describe which LLM calls depend on which results, and the system transforms this into a directed acyclic graph: nodes are model calls or data processing, and edges indicate who receives the results. It then jointly optimizes the entire workflow based on this.

[\"[[O0]]先减少调用。[[C0]] 删除不影响最终输出的节点，合并输入相.en: [[O0]]First, reduce the number of calls.[[C0]] Delete nodes that do not affect the final output, and merge duplicate subprocesses with the same input; for the same input that meets determinism conditions and has been executed before, directly read the cached complete output, skipping that model call.

[\"[[O0]]再减少重复输入计算。[[C0]] 分析 prompt 模板的共.en: [[O0]]Then reduce repeated input computations.[[C0]] Analyze the common prefixes of prompt templates, proactively compute and retain shareable KV for reuse in subsequent calls. Here, the cache is for the model input state, which is different from caching the complete response in the first step.

[\"[[O0]]按缓存与依赖安排执行。[[C0]] 结合模型计算成本、共同前缀.en: [[O0]]Schedule execution based on cache and dependencies.[[C0]] Combine model computation cost, common prefixes, and machine load to decide which GPU to allocate calls to and the order to run them, aiming to use the relevant cache while it is still available.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 在规定好的工作流上，减少调用、缓存输出.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] On a specified workflow, reducing calls, caching outputs, reusing KV, and arranging execution order collectively improve end-to-end latency. The paper limits itself to the same base model, LLM calls, and local data operations, without covering remote tool APIs; therefore, its cost conditions differ from an open-ended coding agent. Tests include Qwen3-8B/14B, H100 NVL, with most experiments using vLLM v0.16.0.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] 一个 Agent 工作流的提示词.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] The prompts, model choices, calling sequence, and tool strategies in an Agent workflow influence each other. Directly having an optimizer modify everything at once makes it difficult to determine why a change is effective. DeCAF breaks optimization into three stages.

[\"[[O0]]Divide：分开探索修改方向。[[C0]] 从同一份初始工作.en: [[O0]]Divide: Explore modification directions separately.[[C0]] Starting from the same initial workflow, assign independent coding Agents for directions such as prompts, models, and workflow structure. Each Agent can only modify its designated scope, is evaluated on the development set, and records candidate solutions and results.

[\"[[O0]]Diagnose：检查修改怎样影响执行。[[C0]] 每个方向.en: [[O0]]Diagnose: Check how modifications affect execution.[[C0]] Each direction retains schemes and experiment records that balance quality, cost, and time differently. During the integration phase, node_eval can also be called to read component inputs, outputs, and execution traces to identify steps that may be dragging down results.

[\"[[O0]]Compose：组合并重新验收。[[C0]] 整合 Agent.en: [[O0]]Compose: Combine and re-evaluate.[[C0]] Integrate the code and discoveries from each Agent to modify the complete workflow. It combines candidate modifications and runs them again on the development set; if performance worsens, adjustments are made based on the diagnosis. The final selected solution is evaluated on a held-out test set.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 在 AppWorld、LiveCode.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] On AppWorld, LiveCodeBench, AgentDojo, and PostTrainBench v1.1, the authors report that the optimized deployment process balances task scores, latency, and cost, but the process of finding a solution itself increases expenses. Controlled fault localization by node_eval can also misidentify downstream affected components as the source, and cannot be regarded as precise causal proof. The multiple agents here are primarily used to optimize another workflow, and the final deployment solution may not include the same number of agents.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] MetaGPT 将软件开发组织成.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] MetaGPT organizes software development into a set of standard operating procedures (SOPs): product managers organize requirements, architects design modules and interfaces, project managers break down implementation tasks, programmers write code, and modifications are made based on execution feedback.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 原文在 HumanEval、MBPP.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] In the original paper, code generation was evaluated on HumanEval and MBPP, and software development, running time, tokens, and manual modification burden were evaluated on SoftwareDev. Structured delivery and execution feedback improved the performance of the tasks measured. These setups include function-level generation and requirement-driven project development, and their results cannot directly represent the efficiency of multiple people simultaneously modifying a real repository.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] Magentic-One 用一个.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] Magentic-One uses a lead to coordinate specialized Agents for web browsing, document reading, coding, and code execution, handling comprehensive tasks that require multiple interaction steps. It is implemented on AutoGen and maintains execution direction through two work logs.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 原文使用 GAIA、Assistant.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The original paper uses GAIA, AssistantBench, and WebArena to cover tasks on real web pages or interactive websites, with model setups including GPT-4o and a combination with o1-preview. Complex tasks benefit from scheduling, progress checking, and replanning, while short tasks may incur additional coordination costs. The paper focuses on general task completion, and it should not be inferred that more roles necessarily lead to faster completion.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] 该工作提出 CAID，让多个工程.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] This work proposes CAID, allowing multiple engineer agents to asynchronously implement tasks in their respective code branches, with a manager arranging work according to dependencies and gradually merging completed code into the main branch.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 主实验使用 Commit0-Lite，.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The main experiment used Commit0-Lite and the Code-Dev protocol from PaperBench to compare single agents with branching-merge teams based on OpenHands, testing Claude 4.5 Sonnet, GLM 4.7, and MiniMax 2.5. The authors report improved task scores, but wall-clock time and cost still need to be considered separately. Code-Dev did not execute the full experimental replication process of the paper, so its scores cannot be considered equivalent to having fully reproduced the paper's results.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] 论文提出 AgentPrune，.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] The paper proposes AgentPrune, which reduces ineffective information transmission in multi-turn discussions. The system treats roles as nodes and message passing as edges: in the same turn, who sends results to whom is one type of edge, and which results from the previous turn carry over to the next turn is another type of edge.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] MMLU、GSM8K、MultiAri.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] Experiments on MMLU, GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP, AQuA, and HumanEval show that part of the communication can be removed while maintaining or improving accuracy and reducing tokens in the tested settings. It optimizes message routing and historical transmission, but searching for the communication structure itself also has a cost. Evaluations focus on QA and function-level code, and information dependencies in long-horizon tool tasks need separate verification.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] AgentDropout 进一步.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] AgentDropout further investigates: besides removing redundant messages, are all roles needed in certain discussion rounds? The same role may be useful in one round but only repeats existing content in another.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 作者在 MMLU、GSM8K、AQuA.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The authors compared Meta-Llama3-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-V3 on MMLU, GSM8K, AQuA, MultiArith, SVAMP, and HumanEval, reporting reduced tokens and improved performance on the tasks tested. "Dynamic" is reflected in different rounds using different member combinations; it includes a graph structure optimization phase and cannot be directly understood as zero-cost during deployment or automatic evaluation of contribution for each message.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] 编排器为每次模型调用附上工作流类.en: [[O0]]Claims and Research Methods:[[C0]] The orchestrator attaches three identifiers to each model call: workflow type, instance, and current role. The gateway strings together requests of the same instance, learning possible role paths and output lengths from historical traces. Predictions are used in three places.

[\"[[O0]]KV 管理。[[C0]] 预测近期还会用到的前缀，将缓存提前搬.en: [[O0]]KV management.[[C0]] Predict prefixes that will be used in the near future and move the cache to faster layers in advance. If the prompt required by the next role can already be constructed, prefill can also be done in advance.

[\"[[O0]]路由与排队。[[C0]] 用输出长度估算单次请求的显存压力，并.en: [[O0]]Routing and queuing.[[C0]] Estimate the GPU memory pressure per request based on output length and consider which calls, when completed, allow downstream tasks to proceed, determining where and when to send the requests.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 论文先观察生产轨迹，再用 AutoGe.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The paper first observes production trajectories, then uses AutoGen to port the internal coding assistant and Deep Research Agent, respectively constructing experimental workloads based on SWE-bench Pro and Deep Research Bench. In cluster experiments, the original frontier model roles are mapped to the Qwen and Llama series ranging from 3B to 14B, with the specific mapping undisclosed. The prototype modifies SGLang's routing, scheduling, and hierarchical caching, measured on 8 A100 80GB GPUs. The authors report that at peak concurrency, average job completion time is reduced to about 1/1.38–1/2.90 of the control, with output throughput 1.12–1.96 times higher. This evidence pertains to service performance; the paper does not verify corresponding changes in software repair pass rates or research report quality. Highly dynamic workflows with unpredictable historical paths may also reduce the benefit of advance preparation.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] 编排层把角色调用顺序表示成 Ag.en: [[O0]]Claims and research methods:[[C0]] The orchestration layer represents the role calling order as an Agent Step Graph. Each request carries the current role and the number of steps until the next call for each role. The inference service uses these step counts to update KV cache nodes corresponding to fixed prompts, prioritizing freeing up caches whose reuse is farther away when GPU memory is tight. When multiple roles share a prefix node, the role that might use it earliest will also be considered.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 原型修改 SGLang v0.4.4.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The prototype modifies the SGLang v0.4.4 frontend and backend. The paper uses Llama-3.1-8B/A10G 24GB and Qwen2.5-32B/H100 80GB to measure synthesized multi-agent workflows and extends this to four-role simulations using PEER Financial QA as input. Compared with SGLang HiCache, the maximum speedup for a single workflow with a long prompt was 1.83×, and the maximum speedup for synthetic high concurrency was 2.19×. For PEER-style workloads, the maximum speedup was 1.08×. For single-workflow experiments, the cache was pre-warmed before measuring the full workflow latency. The paper did not measure answer accuracy.

[\"[[O0]]主张与研究方法：[[C0]] 从一条失败轨迹出发，按执行顺序倒.en: [[O0]]Claims and research methods:[[C0]] Starting from a failed trajectory, the roles are checked backward in execution order. Temporary clues from training answers or acceptance constraints are given to the last role first, reusing outputs from previous roles, and only rerunning that role and its downstream roles. If the final result passes acceptance, this role is marked as a fixable point. Samples that still fail continue to be attempted upstream. That a single role can provide a remedy only indicates that modifying it may be effective; it cannot determine the earliest point of error.

[\"[[O0]]主要结论：[[C0]] 五项基准为 HotpotQA、HoVe.en: [[O0]]Main Findings:[[C0]] The five benchmarks are HotpotQA, HoVer, PUPA, IFBench, and MATH. The first four use GEPA's multi-agent system, partitioning, and reward functions, while MATH uses MACM's setup. Tasks and optimizers share the same foundation, and comparisons are made between GPT-5-mini and Qwen3-8B. Both foundations outperform the control in the average scores across the five benchmarks. Table 4 reports that the average offline optimization time for GPT-5-mini is 136 minutes, compared to 337 minutes for GEPA. Appendix O reports that the experimental server setup includes 4 RTX A6000 GPUs and 256 GB of memory, with the inference engine undisclosed. An answer leakage audit in the paper also found that a small number of final prompts still contain specific content from the training samples.
